nouns-and-adjectives.title: nouns-and-adjectives
nouns-and-adjectives.content:
nouns and adjectives

Adjectives always come after a noun following the "biè", "biē", or "biě" modifiers, meaning "which is", "which could be", and "which is not" respectively.

"toù biè koùrū"

"ball which is red"
"red ball"/ "the ball is red"


Some adjectives are nouns, example "the house is wooden".

In this case we'd use the "which is noun" modifier, "biètoù"

"chǐgà biètoù hoù"

"cave which is noun house"

"the cave is a house"

the-magic-of-suffixes.title: the-magic-of-suffixes
the-magic-of-suffixes.content:
The magic of suffixes

Positivity, degree, amount, and, thus, from, even wanting, are all handled by suffixes.

Suffixes are in everything from

"shìshoǔtsòpǎyaìtiēshiè"

"I want a cat"

to

"toùbièkoùrū"

"the ball is red"

So let's learn about them!





Positivity

New words needed for this:

"tseǐnà", "throw"

"tsaìseī", "happy, sad"


"ma" is the sound used to indicate positivity, there's 4 types

"mà", positive

"mǎ", negative

"mā", neither positive nor negative

"màǎ", could be either positive or negative

Positivity is always the first suffix to be added, and effects the word directly.

"tseǐnàmǎ"

"did not throw"

"tsaìseīmà"

"feel happy"


Occasionally a suffix will not have a negative version, but will still need to transmit that information. Example is the suffix "tsòpǎ" or "want", so how do we say "not want"? This is where the specific "suffix positivity" suffix comes in.

Acting the same way as positivity, "ba" applies to the previously used suffix rather than the attached word.



Examples

"shìshoǔchūbǎ"

"is not mine"

"yǎneǎwībiè pīchù jìmǎ shìshoǔ"

"I don't know if the light is on or off"

"shìyūtsòpaǐbàǎ"

"you might need it"

"tsaìseīmā shìshoǔ"

"I feel apathetic"





Possession

New words needed for this:

"yaìteīshiè", "cat"

"shìzeà", "they"

"sǎtēwà", "computer"

"toù", "ball"

"chaìcheī", "bird"

"shìyǒ", "enemy"

"sheì", "water"


There are five different types of possession, have, take, give, want, and need. Any further types are handled by further suffixes,

"tsòpaǐbǎ"

"don't need"

"tsòpǎ[suffix degree]"

"really want"


"shìyūchū yaìtiēshiè"

"you have a cat"

"shìshoǔyò sǎtēwà"

"I took a computer"

"shìshoǔyǒ toù tēraǐ shìzeà"

"I gave them the ball"

"shìshoǔtsòpǎ chàcheī"

"I want a bird"

"shìshoǔchū shìyòtsòpaǐ sheì"

"my enemy needs water"


Notice how we can chain possessions together, but they only apply to what it's directly connected to.

Some of these used the location aspect, to understand more see the document "Time and Space".





Basic connections

and

There's two ways to say "and", one is related and the other is unrelated.

"shìshoǔchū shìkūpà shìyǒ jì shìshoǔ"

"I know my friend and my enemy"

"shìshoǔchū shìkūjà shìyǒ jì shìshoǔ"

"I know my friend and the enemy"


Notice how "pà" is indicating the enemy is related in my possession, but "jà" is indicating unrelated and thus isn't my enemy.

"pà" is typically the one used, with "jà" only being used if it's needed to specify a disconnection.

tone.title: tone
tone.content:
Tone

Not to be confused with "Tones", the pitches used in the spoken language.


Tone is something that indicates the feeling or intent behind a sentence.

"tsaìbiè wiēnaǐ niè"

"how are you? (polite)"

"shìtsoǔtsòpaǐ [leave] [urgent]"

"we need to leave (urgent)"


Using a tone is always expected, not using one is a good indicator that you're not good at the language.

Tone is always placed at the end of a sentence after the subject, there is no requirement for what tone to use.



Tones can also be stacked on top of each other. For example,

""

[] (confused) + [] (curious) would be exactly that, "confused and curious".


Some tone combinations create new meanings instead of just stacking it, like,
"", "cocky"

[] (questioning) + [] (aggressive)


If you want to literally say you're questioning and aggressive, you can typically just change the tones or pitch of the words, high to flat, flat to low, and low to flat, to separate them.

In more ambiguous cases you can add "tō" to the end to indicate it's separate.

Though it's not proper grammar, very rarely you'll hear people place the word "", "and, also" between it, like ""


Some tones may also be adjectives or even verbs, typically feelings like "happy" or "surprised", which also means you can say any tones separately to convey a feeling.



Most tones are self explanatory, but we'll give some further information for some here, along with a full list, mostly for me to keep track of.

interjections.title: interjections
interjections.content:
Interjections and additives

Interjections and expressions have some weird overlap, and might be a little complex on their own, so let's look into it!


Interjections are the literal definition, a word that is disconnected in meaning from the words around it.

"jàā", "hello"

"", "bye"

"yōō", "oh"
"", "okay"


And so on. These are always placed at the beginning of a sentence,

"jàā tsaìbiè wiēnaǐ niè"

"hello how are you?"

""

"bye, good luck!"

""

"oh, I'm just bored"

""

"okay, I understand"



Expression interjections are named as such because I have no idea what they actually are, and are placed at the end right before the tone.

"tseǐnà gǒsē"

"sorry for throwing it"

"shìyūyǒ [pen] tēraǐ shìshoǔ [please] niè"

"can you please give me the pen?"

"shìshoǔchū [work (noun)] hō nōzě shìyū [thank you] niè"

"thank you for doing my work"

40a84886-6508-4bdf-a02f-d930d5c39a94.title: religion
40a84886-6508-4bdf-a02f-d930d5c39a94.content:
religion

While kidera has mainly forgotten religion, neon city still actively practices it, albeit without the mystical aspects anymore.

But where did this come from?

How did a civilisation based around empirical knowledge form a religion?

And how do they practice it?

The people of kidera practice their religion with a kind of holy book called "[civilisation]{have} [beginning], [nietojie]{have} [life]" "Beginning of civilisation, The life of nietojie"

Summary of the text:

2500 years ago they didn't recognise gender, only sex, but one young girl was so insistent on being a woman they had to accept it.

In her early years she was generally pretty reserved, not being accepted for who she believed herself to be, she spend most of her time alone in the forest. Giving herself the name "woman of the forest", or kHRiefRozie. Her dead name has been lost, intentionally forgotten by the next generation by her request.

Later hearing of issues within the village, she gave her suggestion for fixing it, and it was perfect.

She was chosen as "the one to listen to", or "", and enacted many changes and invented many things.

Under the rule of kHRiefRozie, she invented agriculture, domesticating animals, using trees for use in structures, tools and weapons, professions, and even writing.

She had the idea of using dedicated symbols for each word or concept, so no matter how much the sounds changed, they would still be readable.

her life

born 2500 years ago kHRiefRozie was raised in w small village in what is now the main area of kidera

generally pretty social in her younger years of about 1 - 4, but drawing more reclusive the more people referred to her as a "son" or "boy", regardless of how much she corrected them.

she started spending more time i the woods away from other people, creating things in her spare time like tools or housing

she found a large tree and made it her home, created a ladder to it, the tree still exists today, being held up by wires with a team to take care of it, as has been for 2500 years

on her daily trip back to the village, she noticed someone attempting to create a sculpture out of a recently dead tree, but was struggling with the tools they were using

she went back to her tree and brought back her own tools, for them

amazed at her creation they started paying attention to her much more, still constantly referring to her using boyish terms

eventually she snapped at them, standing on top of a large rock and insisting she was a woman and would not take anything less than pure respect for herself

some people laughed at this, in response she pulled out a bow she had invented and shot them

no one ever dared to challenge her on it after that

Introduction

 hòchoǔsiē is a complex, tonal, and logographic language that primarily relies on suffixes.

The language has 3 tones or pitches, called

  • "high", "kànà", ""

  • "flat", "rānà", ""

  • "low", "naǐnà", ""

Sometimes referred to as "", "", and "" respectively.

"beìkìbiè kànà", "beìkìbiè rānà", and "beìkìbiè naǐnà".

In romanisation the tone is shown through the accent on the last vowel, "à" is high, "ā" is flat, "ǎ" is low.

The language has two writing systems, a logographic one called "", "sōpiěfà-hōtsǒ", and a featural block one called

"", "neàshǔgē-gěrò-hōgǔzeā", commonly referred to as "", "neàgěhō".

The featural block system is used for onomatopoeias, abbreviations, loan words that are not officially added, including names of things outside the language, and using it as a replacement for teaching the language to others or children.

The logographic system is used for everything else.

Featural blocks have the consonant at the top left, tone on the bottom left, and vowel on the right.

  • "kà" > ""

  • "gà" > ""

  • "gì" > ""

  • "gī" > ""

In standard writing, the proper way is vertical (top to bottom, left to right), however it can be written left to right, top to bottom if required or for design aesthetics, commonly done in computers. Neither the sōpiěfàhōtsǒ nor neàgěhō writing systems have spaces.

Romanisation is writing non latin scripts using latin characters, to better allow people to read it.

A glossing is a specific structure using mainly english words to show the word order of a sentence.

  • ""
    "moūcheībiè bǒmǒnà nōhìzě tēshàpìnà shìshoǔ niè"
    "[walk]{which is} [long] [time][yesterday] [location][park] [I] [polite]"

In glossing "[]" indicates a word, and "{}" indicates a suffix. Suffixes are always placed connecting to their words, "[hot]{high}".

All words are separated by a space, "[walk] [I]", unless the first is an article, "[time][yesterday]".

In ambiguous words, their part of speech is displayed beside them, "v[paint]", "o[paint]".

Romanisation is very similar, suffixes and articles connected, words separated.

Sometimes suffixes are separated by a dash to make a 1 to 1 connection with ideograms.

  • ""

  • "shìshoǔ-chū sheì niè"

  • "[I]{have} [water] [polite]"

This does not happen with articles because they don't have a character.

There is 155 ideograms estimated 2200 each with their own word and concept, any words beyond this amount are made of multiple characters.

Each character has a specific way that it's pronounced. This is usually just the word, but they each have a secondary pronunciation for words that use multiple characters, called "multi characters", abbreviated as "mc".

As an example, "" (person) is pronounced "shì", but in "" (government) it's pronounced as "shǐ".

This second pronunciation is called a "combination reading", or "", "hōgǔzeā-haìnā". Abbreviated as "cr".

The base pronunciation for a character is the "singular reading", or "", "hōgǔzeā-tsùraǐyā-fǒ".

Multi characters follow the pattern of describing the word, then removing all suffixes or anything else unnecessary.

They can also be combined into larger words.

  • "" > ""

  • "sà tèwǎ niè" > "sǎtēwà"

  • "" > ""

  • "sòpièfǎ sà cheī-tò sǎtēwà niè" > "sōpiěfàsǎcheìsǎtēwà"

  • "" > ""

  • "shūgēshìjiě-tò shì tě shìtē niè" > "shǔgēshìniēshǐshītē"

Multi characters can be abbreviated, this is usually done by taking only the first sound of each character in it's combination reading. These are commonly written in neàgěhō.

  • "" > ""

  • "sōpiěfàsǎcheìsǎtēwà" > "sōsǎcheìsǎtē"

  • "" > ""

  • "shǔgēshìniēshǐshītē" > "shǔshǐshī"

Many words have a starter point, an initial concept that encompasses all of that category, this is different from a multi character.

As an example "shì" for people, "shà" for plants, "tsaì" for emotions, and so on.

names in hòchoǔsiē are made with the same process as multi characters, but with much more freedom.

If we were to take the name concept "*insert concept here*" could be

  • "*insert name interpretation here*"

  • "*insert name interpretation here*"

  • "*insert name interpretation here*"

  • "*insert name interpretation here*"

and so much more. Dropping the starter point of a name is very common, for the name "", "shǐyaìtièshē", most would drop the starter point in the pronunciation, pronouncing it as "shǐtièshē". However for the name "花", "shǐshàgè", most wouldn't drop anything, as a 3 syllable name is more desirable, though that doesn't mean "shǐgè" isn't a valid pronunciation.

Kidera has a close connection with their culture, and their religion, and as thus many names are connected with these things.

In kidera culture, it's considered extremely disrespectful to use the same name as a famous person, as it's seen as taking the name away from them. This is why the names "woman of the forest", "guy that created kidera's communism", and "guy that tore down oppression (stoic mountain)" are names you will never find, because they belong to extremely important people.

hòchoǔsiē is base 6, going from 1 to 6, stating the smallest number first then going larger.

  • ""

The power is stated first followed by a multiplier, "", "6*2" or 12.

The one's place digit doesn't have a power, because there is no "6^0" character, nor a need for one.

Principle of

Principle of Privacy

Cameras;

  • Security

Cameras can not be placed in a location where the outside world is visible.

Cameras when activated must have a delay which allows the person that activated it to go out of frame before the camera turns on.

  • Example, if it takes 5 seconds to move out of frame, it must take 7 seconds to turn on.

Cameras must only be active if it is unreasonable for a person to be in frame.

  • Example, if it is reasonable for a person to be in a back room during working hours, a camera must not be on during this time.

Definitions

Outside world;

If completely encompassed by walls, ie a location where it is not possible to leave without going through an entry way; a location with access to at least 900 square meters of natural grass, roofing that does not exceed 10% coverage of unaltered access to a directly above sky, and non solid, clear, and non blurry transparent walls, without having to go through a building entry way.

Or if without walls; the ability to traverse anywhere in the world within reason ie excluding the need for tools or vehicles such as boats cars or planes, without having to go through a building entry way.

Building;

A structure which separates the outside world from another location that is not the outside world.

Entry way;

A hole in a wall with a door or gate that must be opened to pass through.
